_notes: KEY NAMING. 433-A keys are prefixed with the printed line marker (1a_full_name, 4f_tp_occupation). 433-A(OIC) PRINTS NO LINE MARKER ANYWHERE ON PAGE 1 - line-markers.mjs reports 0 markers on page 1 of 8, and the first printed marker on the form is (1a) on page 2. So the keys in this slice are prefixed with the printed SECTION number instead: s1_ for 'Section 1 Personal and Household Information', s2_ for 'Section 2 Employment Information for Wage Earners'. From page 2 onward the form does print markers and those keys will follow the marker without its parentheses - printed (32) gives 32_.

THE KEY IS NOT THE PROPERTY NAME. Keys here name cells on this form. Where the same fact already exists in the backbone the crosswalk binds it as exact, and the HubSpot property name comes from the crosswalk, not from the key.

THE INTERNAL NAMES ON THIS FORM ARE SEMANTIC, NOT POSITIONAL, AND FIVE OF THEM ARE WRONG. 433-A's leaf suffixes lag the printed line by exactly one, form-wide, which is a trap that announces itself the moment you count. This form's names carry no line reference at all (75 of 80 marker-attached widgets have no line token; 2 carry one and it agrees; 0 lag), so they read as descriptions - and a description that is wrong reads as right. The five measured so far, none of them in this slice, recorded here because someone will later read the name and try to 'fix' the map: (1) topmostSubform[0].F433-A-OIC_Page6[0].Interest_Dividends[0] is printed line (32), 'Additional sources of income used to support the household' - NOT interest and dividends; (2) topmostSubform[0].F433-A-OIC_Page6[0].tab_order[1].Interest_Dividends[0] is (32)'s 'List source(s)' free text; (3) topmostSubform[0].F433-A-OIC_Page6[0].Interest_Dividends[1] is printed line (33) and IS interest, dividends and royalties - the only true one of the four; (4) topmostSubform[0].F433-A-OIC_Page6[0].tab_order[2].Interest_Dividends[0] is on the EXPENSE half of the page, printed line (50), 'List debt(s)/expense(s)' - seventeen printed lines away from any income; (5) topmostSubform[0].F433-A-OIC_Page2[0].RetirementAcct2[0].CurrentMarketValue[0].Times_7[0] sits under a printed 'X .8 = $' at printed line (3a). Its name says seven; the page says point eight. Binding it by name would print a 0.7 multiplier on a statement signed under penalty of perjury.

NO ALLOWED BLOCK, BY RULING. 433-A prints an 'IRS USE ONLY / Allowable Expenses' column beside every expense line and 433-F prints its Section H equivalent; 433-A(OIC) prints no such column anywhere. Its printed instruction folds the standard INTO the taxpayer's own figure on two lines only - 'For expenses claimed in boxes (39) and (45) only, you should list the full amount of the allowable standard even if the actual amount you pay is less' - and says nothing about it elsewhere. So nothing on this form is auto-filled from irs-standards-2026.json, and this map has no `allowed` key at all.

WHERE NEVER-AUTOFILL LIVES ON THIS MAP. Because there is no `allowed` block, the never-autofill declaration is at the TOP LEVEL as `_never_autofill`, not at `allowed._never_autofill`. verify-form-coverage.mjs accepts either root. The construct itself is unchanged: entries are objects whose `target` is a string, so the schema-agnostic validator checks every one of them for existence, and each is validated and never written.

SLICE BOUNDARY. This slice is the two printed sections that begin and end on page 1, and page 1 carries nothing else. That coincidence of section boundary and page boundary happens nowhere else on this form: Section 3 spans pages 2-4, Section 5 straddles 4-5, Section 6 shares page 5 with the tail of Section 5, and Section 9 spans 7-8. Taking Section 1 alone would have split a page; taking page 1 alone splits nothing, because page 1 is exactly these two sections. 74 of 425 fields.
ROW ORDER IS PRINTED ORDER. household_members binds Row1..Row4 in descending y (324.0, 309.6, 295.2, 280.8), which is the order a person reads them in.

SLICE 2 - THE QUICK SALE TRIPWIRE AT (3a), MEASURED. topmostSubform[0].F433-A-OIC_Page2[0].RetirementAcct2[0].CurrentMarketValue[0].Times_7[0] occupies x 187.2..295.2 at y 219.6. Binding by the name would print 0.7, understating the retirement asset by 10% of its market value on a statement signed under penalty of perjury, and (3), (3a) and every total below would still reconcile.

SLICE 2 - COMPUTED vs NOT CHECKABLE, BY THE PRINTED CAPTION. A cell whose printed caption states a formula ENTIRELY in terms of other cells printed on this page is declared under _computed and is verifiable by recomputation from what the filled PDF prints. A cell whose printed caption sources its figure from an ATTACHMENT is writable input and is declared under _not_checkable with the caption as the reason, because nothing printed on the page could verify it. That one rule settles all of this page's total-shaped cells without a per-case decision. It follows the 433-F Section E footer precedent (433f.totals.json not_checkable.entries[0]) and its converse: rows the form has no slot for are dropped to an attachment and are NOT in a printed total, which is exactly what makes the other totals checkable, so a cell about precisely those dropped rows cannot be.

SLICE 2 - NO adapters/pdf/maps/433aoi.totals.json IS AUTHORED IN THIS SLICE, DELIBERATELY. run-form-gate.mjs step 10 checks a totals file whenever one EXISTS. Its feeder schema can add and it can subtract (a feeder may carry sign: -1); it cannot MULTIPLY and it cannot carry a printed CONSTANT. Two of this page's computed cells need exactly those: (3a) needs Times_7 = current market value X .8, and (1) needs 'Add lines (1a) through (1c) minus ($1,000)'. A totals file authored now would switch step 10 on while being structurally incapable of checking the two cells on this page that most need checking, and the other eight lines would report a clean pass beside them. That is the 'no declared state' condition this repo keeps finding defects in. So the arithmetic is declared here under _computed, verified by read-back in this slice, and step 10 stays SKIPPED with its reason printed until the feeder schema gains a factor and a constant. Recorded for Principal as a TOOL change, not a map change - the same direction of fix as generalising verify-form-coverage.mjs to accept a top-level _never_autofill.

SLICE 2 - NOTHING ON PAGE 2 IS DECLARED EXCLUSIVE, AND THAT IS A DECISION, NOT AN OMISSION. Page 1's option sets are exclusive because the page makes them so: a person is unmarried or married, and 'Do you' is one question with one answer. Page 2 prints THREE option lists - the bank account types on (1a) and (1b), 'Stocks / Bonds / Other' on (2a) and (2b), and '401K / IRA / Other' on (3a) - and prints no 'check one' instruction over any of them. One brokerage account can truthfully hold both stocks and bonds, so declaring that list exclusive would assert a constraint the page does not print and would hard-stop a truthful record. Little is lost: a group slot's checkboxes construct takes ONE input value and checks ONE box, so the read-back still shows exactly one box checked per row, and verify-form-coverage.mjs buckets the rest as 'checkboxes unchecked (independent)', which is an accounted-for state and not a gap. What IS lost is the guard against a box already set in the source PDF. Reported to Principal as arguable rather than resolved: the bank and the retirement lists are very likely exclusive in the world, and this map declines to say so because the page does not.

SLICE 2 - THE TWO BANK ROWS ARE NOT THE SAME SHAPE, AND THE MAP SAYS SO. Printed line (1a) offers SIX account types - Cash, Checking, Savings, Money Market Account/CD, Online Account, Stored Value Card. Printed line (1b) offers FIVE: the same list without Cash. So 1ab_bank_accounts declares six options on slot 0 and five on slot 1 rather than a uniform table, because check-row-shape.mjs reads declaredColumns PER SLOT and a uniform declaration here would be a claim about the page that is false. A record whose SECOND bank row says 'Cash' hard-stops on UNKNOWN CHECKBOX OPTION rather than filing silently under the wrong type or leaving the type blank.

SLICE 2 - equity MEANS TWO DIFFERENT THINGS ON THIS PAGE, SO IT IS TWO COLUMN NAMES. On investments (2a)/(2b) and on life insurance (4a) the printed row is '$ [value] - $ [loan] = $ [line]', so equity = value minus loan, which is the backbone's investment.equity and life_insurance_policy.equity. On retirement (3a) the printed row is '$ [value] X .8 = $ [qsv] - $ [loan] = $ (3a)', so the same-shaped cell is QUICK SALE value minus loan. It is declared as quick_sale_equity, NOT equity, precisely so a future engine computing equity = value - loan uniformly cannot reach it. Giving them one name would make the 20% error a one-line mistake in a shared helper.

SLICE 2 - THE DIGITAL ASSET BLOCK IS BOUND AS SCALARS, NOT AS A GROUP, AND THE REASON IS THE ENGINE. Every other asset block on this page is a group, which buys row_class protection against a row landing in the wrong printed table. The digital asset block cannot be, because its row label carries a LONE checkbox ('Digital asset', box x 36.0..45.0 at y 378.9, printed word at x 50.4..94.0) with no counterpart cell, and fill-433aoi.mjs supports check_here only at the TOP LEVEL, not per group slot. Rather than invent a per-slot construct this slice cannot exercise, the block is bound as 2c_ scalars and its lone box under check_here. The form prints exactly one digital asset row, so nothing is lost today; when Section 9's digital asset questions are read, a per-slot check_here may be worth adding.

THE DEPENDENT TABLE HAS ONE FEWER ROW THAN 433-A's. 433-A's household_members group has five slots because that form prints Row4 twice (Row4[0] and Row4[1] carry the same leaf names). This form prints four rows and enumerates four; max is 4. A fifth household member goes to an attachment - the form has no slot for it, and inventing one would print a person outside the printed rule.

_nesting_note_page2: AcroForm nesting depth is not uniform on page 2 either, and the money cells are where it varies. Institution1[0], Institution2[0] and RetirementAcct2[0] each wrap their value cell in a CurrentMarketValue[0] subform and their loan cell in a LessLoanBal[0] subform, but hang the ROW TOTAL (Total_Current_Market_Value[0]) directly off themselves. CurrentCash[0] uses CurrentCashValue[0] and LessLoanBal1[0] - note the '1'. TotalLife[0] uses TotalLifeIns[0] and LessLoanbal2[0] - note the '2' AND the lower-case 'b'. RetirementAcct1[0] puts its lone checkbox and its description under virtualCurrency[0] but numberOfUnits[0], locationDigitalAsset[0] and assetsAccountNumber[0] directly under itself. check_here._why: A construct this form needs and 433-A does not. Every checkbox set on 433-A pairs an affirmative target with a negative one, so `checkboxes` can always name an option for either answer. This form prints a lone 'check here' box with NO counterpart cell: the negative answer is the box left blank. Modelling it as a yes/no option set would mean inventing a target for 'no', and there is no cell to invent it into. A truthy input checks the box; a falsy input leaves it blank; a value that is neither stops the run rather than being guessed at.

exclusive._note_page_2: NO PAGE-2 SET IS DECLARED HERE, DELIBERATELY. Page 2's three option lists - bank account type on (1a)/(1b), Stocks/Bonds/Other on (2a)/(2b), 401K/IRA/Other on (3a) - print no 'check one' instruction anywhere, and one brokerage account can truthfully hold both stocks and bonds. Declaring them exclusive would assert a constraint the page does not print and would hard-stop a truthful record. A group slot's checkboxes construct takes one input value and checks one box, so the read-back still shows exactly one checked per row; verify-form-coverage.mjs buckets the remainder as 'checkboxes unchecked (independent)', which is a declared state, not a gap. See _notes for the full reasoning and for what this gives up. 2c_digital_asset_held is absent for the same reason s1_community_property_state_last_10_years is: a lone box has nothing to be exclusive with.
exclusive._note: Guard, not a binding. Yes/No pairs and option sets on these forms are INDEPENDENT AcroForm checkboxes - nothing in the PDF stops two of them being checked at once - so the constraint is asserted here and read back off the saved form. Every target below is also bound above; that duplication is the point, and verify-form-coverage.mjs treats this root as a guard so it is not counted as a second binding. s1_community_property_state_last_10_years is deliberately ABSENT: a lone box has nothing to be exclusive with.
